title: Princess Bamba
hookLine: another daughter moved to Lahore and kept the family's memory

lines: A HOUSE FULL OF OLD PORTRAITS.
cards: A house in Lahore, full of old things. Paintings of men in turbans and jewels. Small portraits on ivory.
Pieces of a vanished court, gathered one by one and kept in a city this family once ruled. The woman who gathered them was born in England, raised English, and could have stayed there all her life.
Instead she moved to Lahore, the capital her grandfather Ranjit Singh had ruled, and her father had lost as a boy.

teach.b: Bamba Duleep Singh was Duleep Singh's eldest daughter, Sophia's sister. Like Sophia, she grew up in English houses, far from Punjab, with a father who had been taken from it.
She traveled to Punjab, and in the end she stayed. She married a doctor who taught at the medical college in Lahore, and made her home in the old capital.
For a child of an exiled family, that was a quiet kind of return: not to a throne, but to a street, a house, a city.

Over the years she gathered what she could of her family's past: paintings, portraits, objects from Ranjit Singh's court. After she died, the collection passed into the care of the government in Lahore.
Today it is known by her name, the Princess Bamba Collection, held at the Lahore Fort. A kingdom was gone, its rooms had emptied, and one granddaughter set about gathering up what was left.

The Gurus use the word simran for remembering: holding the Name of God in mind, again and again, so it isn't lost. What Bamba did is not simran in that sense; her remembering was of a family and a court.
But the two share a shape: memory doesn't simply stay.
Somebody keeps it, or it goes. Bamba died in Lahore and is buried there, in the city her family once ruled.

how: Visitors to the Lahore Fort can see the Princess Bamba Collection of Sikh-era paintings and objects, and some Sikh families keep their own memory of the Sikh kingdom in pictures, stories and visits to Lahore.

games.q: you're Bamba. you've seen Punjab, the land your family lost. you could go back to England, where you grew up. what do you do?
o: go back to England and leave the past behind.
stay in Lahore and gather your family's past.
travel on and never settle anywhere.
games.why: she stayed in Lahore, married there, and gathered paintings and objects from her grandfather's court into a collection.

practice: Bring to mind one thing from your family that could easily be lost, a recipe, a saying, a story about a grandparent, a photo in a drawer, a song somebody hummed, and look at it closely, the way Bamba might have held a portrait.
Ask who else knows it; if nobody does, it's yours to keep. If you pray, Waheguru can keep you company while you look.

wordCard.voice: Princess Bamba. Bamba Duleep Singh, Duleep's eldest daughter, who made her home in Lahore and gathered her family's past into a collection that bears her name. Today's word.
